newsitem.title: UK: Burton casts UK spring fashion spree doubts.
newsitem.headline: Burton casts UK spring fashion spree doubts.

text.p: Disappointing sales at Burton Group Plc's multiple fashion stores over the past 10 weeks cooled expectations for a bumper spring season for UK clothing retailers, analysts said on Thursday.

Burton, owner of Dorothy Perkins and Top Shop, reported an 11 percent increase in sales overall in the 10 weeks to May 10. Department store Debenhams did better than expected with 10.9 percent, exculding mail order, but sales at the fashion stores were below forecasts at just three percent.

Retail analysts said the sales momentum at Principles, Top Shop and Dorothy Perkins had not been as good as expected, which suggested rivals Next Plc and Marks & Spencer Plc may also fall short of expectations. M&S, which reports annual results next week, saw its shares slip 11.5 pence to 508 pence and Next's were 15.5 pence lower at 692.

Burton's shares came under pressure despite a 23 percent increase in first half profits as there was widespread disappointment on the current sales from the multiple fashion chains. They were 7.5 pence lower at 146.5 by 1230 GMT.
"I think we might find the last four weeks for womens clothing has not been easy," said one retail analyst.
Analysts said Burton's current sales performance would prompt adjustments to top-of-the-range profit forecasts for the current year, which were around 190 million stg down to about 185 million.
"What Burton said gives pause for thought. Maybe the clothing market hasn't been as strong as people thought," said retail analyst Nick Bubb at MeesPierson.
The market was strong in March, helped by mild weather, but the trend seems to have reversed in May, analysts said.

Burton's results also disappointed investors who still perceive the company as a recovery stock. Analysts said the results suggested the group's rapid recovery phase from troubles in recession of the early 1990s had come to an end.
"For what a lot of people still see as a recovery stock it's not a particularly robust top line," said another analyst, who asked not to be named.

The overall picture will be clearer by the end of next week after M&S results, followed by Storehouse Plc's on Thursday. Next is also expected to give a current trading update at its annual meeting on Friday.
This could put Burton's performance in context and the share price fall, which analysts considered to be overdone, could be reversed. they said.
